{
  "IP": "neorv32_debug_auth",
  "Conceptual Assets": [
    {
      "Concept ID": "C1",
      "Concept Name": "Authentication write value",
      "Unit": "neorv32_debug_auth",
      "Information": "The one-bit authentication value consumed from the write data determines whether authentication is accepted. It is not returned as data, but the authentication result can expose this value indirectly.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "yes",
        "Integrity": "no",
        "Availability": "no",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "The authentication value is consumed at line 57 and affects valid_o through authenticated_q at line 66, so observing the status can reveal the accepted value.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "C"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could observe valid_o while probing authentication values to infer the authentication value.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "wdata_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [
        57
      ],
      "Held Lines": [],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C2",
      "Concept Name": "Authentication-valid state",
      "Unit": "neorv32_debug_auth",
      "Information": "The one-bit state records whether authentication is currently valid, and authenticated debug operation depends on this result. It is reported to the surrounding debug logic through valid_o.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "authenticated_q is reset, cleared by enable_i, or overwritten from wdata_i under we_i at lines 52, 55 and 57, so unauthorized changes can corrupt the authentication result.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could write a false authentication value or clear authenticated_q so that valid_o falsely authorizes or disables debug access.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "wdata_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [
        "valid_o"
      ],
      "Entry Lines": [
        57
      ],
      "Held Lines": [
        52,
        55,
        57
      ],
      "Exit Lines": [
        66
      ]
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C3",
      "Concept Name": "Authentication enable control",
      "Unit": "neorv32_debug_auth",
      "Information": "The enable control determines whether the authentication state is retained or cleared. It controls whether authentication can remain valid.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "enable_i directly controls the clear assignment to authenticated_q at lines 54-55, so changing it can corrupt the authorization state.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could force enable_i low to clear authentication and keep valid_o deasserted, disabling authenticated debug operation.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "enable_i"
      ],
      "Leaves Through": [],
      "Entry Lines": [
        54
      ],
      "Held Lines": [],
      "Exit Lines": []
    },
    {
      "Concept ID": "C4",
      "Concept Name": "Authentication write command",
      "Unit": "neorv32_debug_auth",
      "Information": "The write command determines whether the incoming authentication value is applied to the authentication state. It is the access decision for changing authentication.",
      "Rubric": {
        "Confidentiality": "no",
        "Integrity": "yes",
        "Availability": "yes",
        "Undermined Expected Behavior": "no"
      },
      "Rubric Reason": "we_i gates the assignment of wdata_i into authenticated_q at lines 56-57, so an unauthorized write command can change or prevent the authentication update.",
      "Objectives At Risk": [
        "I",
        "A"
      ],
      "Attack": "An attacker could assert we_i with a chosen write value or suppress it to forge or block an authentication update.",
      "Enters Through": [
        "we_i"
      ],

        56
      ],

      "Exit Lines": []

  ],
  "Not Kept": [
    {

    {
      "Candidate Name": "Busy status",
      "Candidate Unit": "neorv32_debug_auth",

conceptual assets.information: The one-bit authentication value consumed from the write data determines whether authentication is accepted. It is not returned as data, but the authentication result can expose this value indirectly.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: The authentication value is consumed at line 57 and affects valid_o through authenticated_q at line 66, so observing the status can reveal the accepted value.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could observe valid_o while probing authentication values to infer the authentication value.

conceptual assets.information: The one-bit state records whether authentication is currently valid, and authenticated debug operation depends on this result. It is reported to the surrounding debug logic through valid_o.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: authenticated_q is reset, cleared by enable_i, or overwritten from wdata_i under we_i at lines 52, 55 and 57, so unauthorized changes can corrupt the authentication result.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could write a false authentication value or clear authenticated_q so that valid_o falsely authorizes or disables debug access.

conceptual assets.information: The enable control determines whether the authentication state is retained or cleared. It controls whether authentication can remain valid.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: enable_i directly controls the clear assignment to authenticated_q at lines 54-55, so changing it can corrupt the authorization state.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could force enable_i low to clear authentication and keep valid_o deasserted, disabling authenticated debug operation.

conceptual assets.information: The write command determines whether the incoming authentication value is applied to the authentication state. It is the access decision for changing authentication.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: we_i gates the assignment of wdata_i into authenticated_q at lines 56-57, so an unauthorized write command can change or prevent the authentication update.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could assert we_i with a chosen write value or suppress it to forge or block an authentication update.

considered, not kept.reason: re_i is never read at line 26 and rdata_o is tied to zero at line 69, so no meaningful information or protected response is transferred.
busy_o is assigned a constant at line 63 and does not represent operational state or a status that affects behavior.
clk_i and rstn_i only time or reset authenticated_q at lines 51-53, and the clocks-and-resets rule excludes them as conceptual assets.
Only the authentication value used at line 57 affects the design; the remaining write-data bits have no RTL use or security mechanism.
